answer_core:
Do not choose the Silva path yet, and do not default to the safer lab path. First turn both options into conditions that can be tested.

For Silva, the unknowns are concrete: data access, sharing terms, collaborator role, timeline, and advisor support. Until those conditions are real, the path is exciting but not yet executable as a dissertation.

For the fallback, the unknown is whether it will still be alive when needed. Work backward from the proposal deadline and stop date: the fallback has to remain advisor-backed, funded, technically ready, identity-coherent, and available if the Silva probe fails.

The next move is not a full proposal. Sequence it: advisor first, short Silva evidence probe second, committee only after the data path is real. Use broad success rates as humility checks, not probabilities for this case. Do not run all options in parallel; define the tests that would make one path executable.
